Earth: Magnetopause

solar wind: pressed in by day, trailing a long tail by night.

Bz 0.0 nT, dynamic pressure 2.0 nPa
Drawn to 120 deg from the nose, as far as the paper
plots its model. That is where the drawing stops, not where
the surface ends: it widens down the tail without limit.
Not tilted: the model is symmetric about the Sun line.

scene/Earth: Rotation Axis and Equator:
Earth: Rotation Axis and Equator

North pole up the gold line; the ring is the equator on the crust.
Tilt from the ecliptic pole (this frame's z): 23.44 deg,
derived from the served pole and the renderer's mean obliquity.
Axis drawn to 7,827 km (0.0000523 AU) -- a drawing length.

The curved arrows at both ends show the sense of the turning:
prograde, west to east, counter-clockwise seen from above the
north pole. This scene is one epoch: the axis is the line Earth
turns about; the turning itself is not shown, and no rotation
period is stated because none is served.

scene/Earth: Terminator (day-night line):
Earth: Terminator (day-night line)

The white circle is where the Sun is on the horizon: the sunlit half
of Earth faces the Sun line, the night half faces away. The yellow
line through the circle's centre is the Sun direction; its dot on
the crust is the subsolar point, where the Sun is overhead.

FROZEN at 2026-09-09. The real terminator
sweeps around Earth once a day; this scene does not turn. Geometry
only -- no lighting is modelled, and the refraction and solar-disc
corrections that define sunrise on the ground are not applied.

info "i" button top right.
scene/moon#4:
Moon: trusted arc of the orbit

The brighter arc is the part of the Moon's orbit where this page's
propagation is trusted to within 0.5 deg: 3.42 days either side of the
elements' epoch.
The arc runs from 2026-09-05 13:00 to 2026-09-12 10:00 (UTC).
There is no longer span to choose: this scene is one epoch, and the
arc is the stretch of orbit the served elements are trusted for.
The faint full ellipse is the same orbit swept once around; outside
the arc, the Moon's real path drifts from it as the Sun and Earth's
shape perturb the two-body orbit.



For more information and references please click on the
info "i" button top right.
